question: Which policy reform targeted improving competitiveness and efficiency of the banking system after 1991?

options.text: Introduction of prudential norms and CRAR
Limiting foreign entry into retail banking

solution:
The correct answer is __**Introduction of prudential norms and CRAR**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In 1991, India initiated banking sector reforms to address inefficiencies and improve the competitiveness of the financial system.
 
• Prudential norms were introduced to ensure banks maintain financial discipline, including provisions for Non-Performing Assets (NPAs).
 
• The Capital to Risk-weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR) was mandated to ensure adequate capitalization of banks, aligning with international Basel norms.
 
• These measures were a part of the Narasimham Committee recommendations aimed at modernizing and strengthening the banking structure.
 
• Implementation of these norms enhanced transparency, improved asset quality, and boosted public confidence in the banking system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prudential Norms:** These are guidelines to ensure financial stability, including rules for income recognition, asset classification, and provisioning for NPAs.
 
• **CRAR (Capital Adequacy Ratio):** It is a measure of a bank's capital in relation to its risk-weighted assets, ensuring the bank can absorb a reasonable amount of loss.
 
• **Narasimham Committee:** A high-level committee formed in 1991 to reform the Indian financial system, focusing on deregulation, reducing government interference, and improving efficiency.
 
• **Basel Norms:** International banking regulations established by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, aimed at strengthening global financial stability.
 
• **Impact of Reforms:** The introduction of these reforms led to improved profitability, better risk management practices, and increased integration of Indian banks with the global financial system.
